title: 49ers lose shot at breaking NFL record for most miles traveled due to Week 11 travel detour en route to Mexico - CBS Sports
description: The 49ers are taking a detour in Week 11 that's going to cost them the NFL record for most miles traveled
body:
The 49ers are taking a detour in Week 11 that's going to cost them the NFL record for most miles traveled
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 20, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:51 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        With a trip to Australia in Week 1 and a trip to Mexico City in Week 11, the expectation before the season started was that the 49ers were going to break the NFL record for most miles traveled this season, but that's actually not going to happen due to a travel detour that the team is taking this week. After beating the Cowboys in Week 10, the 49ers didn't fly home to California. Instead, they took a flight to Colorado, where they spent the week getting acclimated to the high altitude in Mexico City, which sits at an elevation of 7,350 feet. The 49ers' decision to head to Colorado will reduce the total number of miles the team travels this year. If the 49ers had flown home after their game against the Cowboys, they would have traveled a total of 2,876 miles round trip. After that, their round-trip flight to Mexico City would have covered 3,702 miles for a two-week total of 6,578 miles. However, since the 49ers didn't fly home after playing the Cowboys, that will lead to a drastic change in their mileage total. Here's what their Week 10 to Week 11 travel will look like (the 49ers fly out of San Jose): 
San Jose to Dallas (1,438 miles)Dallas to Colorado Springs (592)Colorado Springs to Mexico City (1,376)Mexico City to San Jose (1,851)Total for all four: 5,257 milesThe decision to practice in Colorado this week will cut their total travel by 1,321 miles this year, trimming their season total from 38,105 miles to 36,784. At that number, they won't set the NFL's mileage record. The Los Angeles Chargers set the record for most travel miles last season when they flew 37,086 miles, and that record will stand for at least another year thanks to the 49ers' decision to take a pit stop in Colorado before heading to Mexico City in Week 11. 
That being said, the 49ers will be setting one NFL record when they take the field on Sunday: They'll become the first team in NFL history to play two international games in two different countries in non-consecutive weeks. The Vikings played in Ireland and England last season, but that came in back-to-back weeks. The 49ers' two international trips are coming 10 weeks apart.

title: MLB rumors: Yankees moves heating up, plus latest on Tarik Skubal, Mets, Padres, Red Sox, more - CBS Sports
description: Here are the latest news and rumors in the MLB offseason on Friday, Nov. 20
body:
Here are the latest news and rumors in the MLB offseason on Friday, Nov. 20
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 20, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:33 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The uncertain 2026-27 Major League Baseball offseason is fully underway. The ongoing CBA negotiations and the near-certainty of an owner-implemented lockout on Dec. 2 loom over all, and it may indeed mean a flurry of trades and free-agent signings leading up to that date. That was certainly the case leading up to the last lockout of 2021-22, and this time around we've already seen some leading examples.  Thanks to that prospect of a hastened pace, offseason rumors are flowing. Speaking of which, we'll be here each day to round up what's out there. You can find Friday's supply just below. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
     Mets made Tarik Skubal a record offer? 
The buzz at the GM Meetings last week was that the Mets offered top free agent Tarik Skubal a nine-year contract worth almost $400 million, reports MLB Network Radio. If the deal is worth at least $390 million, it would set new records for total guarantee and average annual value given to a pitcher. Here are the current pitcher contract records: Total GuaranteeAverage annual value1. Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Dodgers: $325M 				1. Max Scherzer, Mets: $43.3M 				2. Gerrit Cole, Yankees: $324M 				2. Justin Verlander, Mets: $43.3M 				3. Stephen Strasburg, Nationals: $245M 				3. Zack Wheeler, Phillies: $42M 				4. Max Fried, Yankees: $218M 				4. Framber Valdez, Tigers: $38.3M 				5. David Price, Red Sox: $217M 				5. Jacob deGrom, Rangers: $37M 				Given the player and the deep-pocketed teams involved in the bidding (Blue Jays, Dodgers, Mets, etc.), Skubal is well-positioned to shatter Yamamoto's record. He could beat Scherzer's and Verlander's record as well. The expected lockout will begin after the collective bargaining agreement expires at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1. Skubal is likely to sign before then.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Red Sox send Oviedo to D-backs
The Diamondbacks are set to acquire righty Johan Oviedo from the Red Sox for minor-league lefty Luke Dotson and a player to be named later, reports the Arizona Republic. Boston had four pitchers for the No. 5 starter's spot (Oviedo, Brayan Bello, Kutter Crawford, Tanner Houck) and always seemed likely to trade one to ease the logjam.Acquired from the Pirates last offseason, Oviedo made just one ineffective appearance around elbow trouble in 2026. He returned from Tommy John surgery in 2025 and looked excellent, and Arizona will hope Oviedo rediscovers that magic as he gets further away from his injuries. Dotson is not a top prospect. It's a low-cost flier for the D-backs. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Tigers lock up Troy Melton
The Tigers have signed right-hander Troy Melton to a six-year extension worth $46.5 million, reports ESPN. There is a club option for a seventh year and escalators can push the total guarantee to $80 million. Melton still had five years of team control. The new extension buys out his five team control years and one free agent year with an option for another free agent year.Melton, 26 next month, missed the start of the season with elbow inflammation and finished the season on the injured list with more elbow woes. Between injuries, he made 20 starts with a sub-3.00 ERA with strong under-the-hood numbers. The Tigers know him better than anyone and are obviously comfortable with Melton's medicals to lock him up long-term.
                            
    
                                                
                    
     Yankees reunite with Jonathan Loáisiga The New York Yankees have agreed to a two-year contract with veteran right-hander Jonathan Loáisiga, ESPN reports. The deal also includes a club option for 2029 and is worth roughly $18 million, according to MLB.com.  
Loáisiga, 32, is coming off that strong season above for the Arizona Diamondbacks, and for his career boasts an ERA+ of 128 across parts of nine MLB seasons. He's worked in relief for almost all of that span, and eight of those nine seasons came with the Yankees.  
                            
    
                                                
                    
     Yankees getting calls on Jasson Domínguez 
New York Yankees general manager Brian Cashman was recently asked if he'd be willing to play Spencer Jones in center field. In response, he told media, including SNY, this:  "I would be comfortable with that. At the same time Jasson Domínguez is pounding the ball in winter ball. The entire industry is noticing that based on the phone calls I'm getting." 	The 23-year-old Domínguez still has big-time power potential, and defensively he's best suited to center field. For his career in the Bronx, he has an OPS+ of 93, but his 751 plate appearances have been doled out erratically across four seasons. As things stand now, he'll once again be subject to a playing-time crunch. Aaron Judge and Cody Bellinger are installed at the outfield corners, and Giancarlo Stanton, if healthy, should get much of the playing time at DH. That leaves center field for Jones or Domínguez. Other teams no doubt see that bottleneck and are seeing if Cashman and the Yankees are willing to relieve it through trade.  
                            
    
                                                
                    
     Padres meet with Skubal 
Lefty ace and two-time American League Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal remains far and away the top talent on the free-agent market. While the New York Mets and incumbent Los Angeles Dodgers seem like the favorites to secure his services, the San Diego Padres also have significant interest in him. That interest took the next step on Thursday with an in-person meeting, The Athletic reports. The Padres are the fourth team to meet with Skubal, who turned 30 on Friday. Previously, the Dodgers, Mets, and Toronto Blue Jays met with him.  The Padres have a pronounced need in the rotation, especially if free-agent right-hander Michael King signs elsewhere. Last winter, they also lost Dylan Cease to the Blue Jays via free agency.  

                            
    
                                                
                    
     Padres extend Gavin Sheets 
The Padres and left-handed platoon hitter Gavin Sheets have agreed to a three-year, $11 million contract extension that includes two opt-outs, FanSided reports. Sheets, who'll turn 31 in April, had been slated for free agency after the upcoming season. Instead, he and the Padres will now be potentially committed through the 2029 season, depending on whether Sheets exercises any of his opt-outs. While he's not much of a hitter for average, he does draw walks and hit for power. In two seasons with San Diego, he's tallied 36 home runs and 44 doubles in 855 at-bats while seeing DH, first base, and the outfield corners.  
                            
    
                                                
                    
     Mets sign Darwinzon Hernández The New York Mets have agreed to a three-year, $12 million deal with right-handed reliever Darwinzon Hernández, reports José F. Rivera.  Hernández, who turns 30 in December, hasn't pitched in MLB since 2022 and instead has revived his career with four strong seasons in Japan. Over that span for Softbank of the NPB, he's put up an ERA of 2.46 in 131 ⅔ innings with 168 strikeouts and 42 unintentional walks. Prior to rebuilding himself in Japan, Hernández had a 5.06 ERA and a 1.82 K/BB ratio over parts of four seasons with the Boston Red Sox.

body:
Fulwiley is still facing three misdemeanors stemming from an incident after an LSU football game
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 20, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:46 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        LSU guard MiLaysia Fulwiley was arrested last Saturday and charged with five counts following an incident with a police officer who was directing traffic after an LSU football game in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. Fulwiley, accused of striking a police officer in a car and fleeing the scene, took to social media to deny the allegations before quickly deleting those posts.The two most serious charges against Fulwiley -- aggravated battery with a dangerous weapon and aggravated assault with a dangerous weapon -- were dropped by District Attorney Hillar Moore on Friday, per WAFB. Both charges were felonies. 
        
            
                LSU guard MiLaysia Fulwiley not with team in first game since arrest, Kim Mulkey stays quiet about status
                
                    Jack Maloney                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Her other three charges -- flight from an officer, resisting an officer and disobedience to police officers -- are all misdemeanors and remain for now. However, Moore said that they will be dismissed if she completes a pretrial diversion program. Fulwiley released a statement on Friday apologizing for her actions and social media posts.
"Saturday night ended in a situation that never should have happened, and my posts afterward made it worse. For that, I owe an apology to the officers involved and everyone who calls themselves a Tiger. I also want to apologize to my family and all those who love and support me," she said."People see the purple and gold before they see me, and I want to carry myself in a way that's worthy of it, on the court and off. Rules and laws apply to everyone, including the instructions of officers working a game night in Baton Rouge. I respect the job those officers do, and I'll let the legal process run its course. My focus is doing what this program asks of me and earning back the trust of the people who count on me."Fulwiley was not with LSU for its two games this week, and coach Kim Mulkey declined to comment on her status. LSU social media accounts did not acknowledge Fulwiley's inclusion on the John Wooden Award Top 50 Watch List this week.Fulwiley played her freshman and sophomore seasons at South Carolina before transferring to LSU. She has won back-to-back SEC Sixth Player of the Year awards and is currently projected as a top 10 pick in the 2027 WNBA Draft. 
Through her first four games this season, Fulwiley is averaging 17.8 points, 3.5 rebounds, 4.3 assists, 4.3 steals and 2.8 blocks on 54.9% shooting. LSU is off to a 6-0 start and is ranked No. 9 in the country.

title: Royce Lewis trade grades: Dodgers land former No. 1 pick; Twins get another arm, arrow-up prospect - CBS Sports
description: Minnesota added right-hander Bobby Miller and catching prospect Francisco Espinoza in return
body:
Minnesota added right-hander Bobby Miller and catching prospect Francisco Espinoza in return
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 20, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:10 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Los Angeles Dodgers have added a former No. 1 overall pick. The Dodgers are set to acquire infielder Royce Lewis from the Minnesota Twins for right-hander Bobby Miller and minor-league catcher Francisco Espinoza, reports the New York Post. Neither team has announced the trade.Lewis, 27, was a candidate to be non-tendered prior to Friday's deadline. Rather than cut him loose, the Twins were able to find a trade partner and receive something in return. The No. 1 pick in the 2017 draft has battled injuries throughout his career and posted a .288 on-base percentage the last three years. Lewis simply failed to launch with Minnesota.
The Dodgers figure to use Lewis as a platoon partner for Max Muncy at third base and could also move him around the infield as a utility guy. The Twins moved him from third base to first base this past season. Lewis has played every infield position in the big leagues, though he's had only one inning at shortstop since 2022.Miller, 27, has been unable to build on his dynamic 2022 rookie season, when he threw 124 ⅓ innings with a 3.76 ERA. He has battled injuries and control issues since then, and the Dodgers moved him into the bullpen this past season. Miller has a 7.75 ERA in 134 ⅔ Triple-A innings the last three years and can be optioned down in 2027.
Espinoza, 19, reached Low Class-A in 2026 and hit .317/.411/.422 with three home runs and strong contact rates in 46 games. He does not rank among the top 30 Dodgers prospects at Baseball America or MLB Pipeline, but Espinoza is an arrow-up prospect and a solid return for a non-tender candidate.Here now are our grades for the two-for-one trade.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Los Angeles Dodgers: AAt worst, Lewis will be a high-priced utility guy next season. He's projected to make $5 million or so through arbitration and that simply is not much for the Dodgers, who have a history of getting underperforming hitters to the next level (like Muncy). At best, Lewis could be the new Chris Taylor and reach his offensive ceiling while bouncing between positions.Espinoza is a good prospect, not a great prospect, and Miller is a reclamation project. Those are easy players for the Dodgers to surrender to take a chance on Lewis and his upside. It may not work. Lewis could continue to get hurt and not hit, but it was a low-cost move and the chance of a reward is significant. 
It's a very nice upside play for a team that has hit on a lot of upside plays over the year.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Minnesota Twins: AIt's a bummer things didn't work out for Lewis and the Twins, but the reality is he was a non-tender candidate, and it wasn't a secret. Minnesota was able to get back a solid prospect in Espinoza and a lottery ticket arm in Miller despite having little leverage. Getting two players for Lewis is a very good outcome under the circumstances.
Giving each team an "A" suggests a win-win, and maybe it will be. There's a chance it's a lose-lose, though. Lewis may not hit, Miller may never rediscover his 2022 form, and Espinoza may not pan out. I see the vision for both teams, though and like it. 
The Dodgers rolled the dice on a talented player and the Twins were able to fetch two players for someone they might have otherwise cut loose and sent into free agency.

There are two lines of thought when it comes to guys who have been out for a while. One, they have fresh legs. Two, they need to shake the rust off or work their way back. On Thursday, we saw what looked like fresh legs as David Montgomery had his best rushing game of the season in his return. Hopefully we see more performances like that the rest of the weekend. Kenneth Walker ruled outThe Chiefs are huge favorites against the Cardinals and play the Bills on Thanksgiving, so it makes sense to give Walker another week. Emmett Johnson is once again a must-start running back and my number two running back overall in full PPR leagues. Brock Bowers was present at practice on ThursdayWe don't think this was a full practice, but it is fantastic news that he was there at all after leaving Week 10 with an ankle injury. We are projecting Bowers to play this week, which of course makes him a must-start tight end. You may want to pick up Michael Mayer just in case, as Mayer would be a borderline top 12 tight end if Bowers is ultimately unable to go.Baker Mayfield returned to practice on ThursdayMayfield missed Wednesday but got a limited session in on Thursday. While the vibe early in the week was negative, we're now prepared to project Mayfield as in on Sunday. That doesn't mean we want to start him. What it does mean is that Bucky Irving is a must-start RB1, and Emeka Egbuka is an upside WR3. Still, if you picked up Jalon Daniels in a Superflex league, you should hold him just in case.
DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks trending towards returnSmith and Wicks were both at practice on Wednesday and Smith sounds like someone who will play. If he does, he's the only Eagles wide receiver we want to start, and he'll be ranked as a WR2. If Smith needs one more week, then Makai Lemon is in play as a borderline WR2 in full PPR. Joe Milton is still expected to start at quarterback, so we won't get too excited about anyone in this passing game. For what it's worth, we like Dallas Goedert more without Smith than with him, but he's a top 12 tight end either way.Darren Waller and Tommy Tremble both questionableWaller and Tremble both got limited sessions in on Thursday and Friday. Since Week 8, Bryce Young has thrown 34.7% of his passes to tight ends, so either of these could be used in a pinch. We'll view Waller as a borderline top-12 tight end if he is active. If Waller is out, then Tremble is a high-end TE2. If either misses, it could be a boost to Jalen Coker, who has seen his target share shrink as the tight ends got more involved. Jonathon Brooks is also questionable, but we don't expect him to have a meaningful role even if he's active.Roman Wilson and Michael Pittman questionableThe biggest impact here is a big blow to Germie Bernard, who falls outside of the top 40 receivers. We are ranking Wilson as a low-end WR3 and DK Metcalf as a borderline WR2. If the Steelers have success running the ball against Philadelphia, it may turn out that you do not want to start any of the Steelers' pass catchers. We would like to see Pittman do something positive before we even think about putting him in our lineup.
Jordan Addison out, T.J. Hockenson and Jauan Jennings backAddison had surgery on his thumb. He won't go on IR, but he definitely won't play this week. That could make Jennings more interesting in a revenge game, but Jennings has shown nothing this year that would make you want to trust him. With Hockenson back, we will rank him as a top 12 tight end. This is a small boost for Kirk Cousins, who is a low-floor streamer.Geno Smith attempting to play, Omar Cooper and Isaiah Williams outI am not sure Smith will get in a full session this week but he has said he plans to play through his ankle injury. We don't really want to start him, but would much rather start Garrett Wilson and Breece Hall if he plays. Adonai Mitchell is also a good boom/bust WR3 assuming Smith plays. Mitchell gets a boost with the decrease. If Cade Klubnik has to start, we will downgrade the entire Jets offense.Jacory Croskey-Merritt practicing in fullWe are expecting Croskey-Merritt to return on Monday night but we have no idea how touches will be distributed between him, Rachaad White, and Austin Ekeler. Unless you are in a truly desperate situation, we would like to avoid all three. If you must, we are ranking them White, Crockey-Merritt, and Ekeler in that order. The first two are high-end flexes while Ekeler is only for the most desperate of managers.
Dalton Kincaid doubtfulThe tight end position looks even more like a disaster with Kincaid likely out. Dawson Knox could be a deep steamer at the position, but we don't have much faith in him, especially since the Bills are huge favorites and may not throw many passes. This could be a small boost in targets for Khalil Shakir, who is a low-end WR3.Josh Johnson preparing to start for Carson BeckThe Arizona Cardinals nightmare continues. While it is never a good thing to start your fourth different QB, I am not sure there will be a huge drop-off from what Beck was going to give us. You can be as nervous as you want about Trey McBride; there's no sitting him. We don't really want to start anyone else from this offense but Zonovan Knight is our favorite flex if you are absolutely desperate.Mike Evans trending towards questionableThe 49ers have a huge game this week against the Vikings, so it wouldn't be surprising if Evans pushes to play. How much he plays is another question altogether. I think the safest way to view Evans is as an upside WR3 if he gives it ago. We would be much less interested in starting Keenan Allen and Deebo Samuel if Evans returns. What's worse is this is a Sunday night game, so you'll need a backup plan if you are waiting out any of these guys.
Ladd McConkey limitedMcConkey has a chance to play this week but we aren't sure if we want him to. He's been terribly frustrating for Fantasy managers and will probably rank as an upside WR3 if he's active. Tre Harris is a Wr3 without McConkey but we would have a hard time starting him if the team's WR1 returns.

title: Colts waive Daniel Jones: Indy not trading QB or Jonathan Taylor at deadline now a major second-guess - CBS Sports
description: Indy has put themselves in a very tough spot after sitting on the fence at the deadline.
body:
Indy has put themselves in a very tough spot after sitting on the fence at the deadline.
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 20, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:43 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Mobb Deep said it best: "Ain't no such thing as halfway crooks." The Indianapolis Colts tried to sit on the fence at the 2026 trade deadline, ship away some (not all) expendable pieces, and land a somewhat respectable, middle-of-the-road record that might save a few jobs in the process. That meant moving on from the likes of DeForest Buckner, Quenton Nelson, and Josh Downs, but holding on to Jonathan Taylor and Daniel Jones. Less than two weeks removed from that semi-fire sale, it's safe to say Indy botched it. What's the old saying? If you're going to be a bear, be a grizzly. Well, if the Colts felt alright selling some pieces at the deadline, they should've stripped it down to the studs, knowing full well they are entering a rebuild anyway after firing GM Chris Ballard in mid-October. The losses have only continued to pile up for the Colts, which includes a demoralizing defeat at the hands of the Houston Texans in Week 11. That game, which dropped them to 3-8, proved to be the straw that broke the camel's back for the Daniel Jones era, as the team has since waived the veteran quarterback. 
Again, this is a player who teams were reportedly interested in leading up to the deadline. Instead of pursuing those opportunities to shed a sunk-cost under center, ESPN reports that Indy rebuffed trade interest from teams like the Minnesota Vikings and Baltimore Ravens. 
As a reminder, the Vikings traded a 2027 third-round pick to acquire Kirk Cousins, while the Ravens shipped a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 seventh-round pick to the Cardinals in exchange for Jacoby Brissett and a 2027 fifth-round pick. It's unclear what the compensation for Jones would've been, but I can tell you this—it's more than what they have now after waiving him: nothing.  In the nine games before the deadline, Jones had the Colts at 2-7 while completing 60.3% of his passes, averaging just 191.3 passing yards per game, and posting a passer rating of 68.9. In total, Jones had tallied seven touchdowns and 13 turnovers. Daniel Jones prior to 2026 trade deadlineStatsTeam record2-7Completion percentage60.3%Passing YPG191.3Pass TDs6INTs10Yards per attempt5.7Air yards per attempt4.6Passer rating68.9Ruhsing YPG17.4Rushing TDs1Fumbles lost3It was abundantly clear in the lead-up to the deadline that the two-year, $88 million extension the Colts signed Jones this offseason to was a disaster. Miraculously, a lifeboat drifted by them in the form of multiple teams inquiring about taking that burden off their hands, but they decided to stay on the deserted island. Now they're paying the price, with Jones set to account for $35.2 million in dead cap space for 2027 (provided he clears waivers) while the team pays him $49.8 million for 11 games played this season. On top of Jones, Taylor, arguably the most sought-after prize on the trade market this cycle, should've been firmly on the block. With the Colts now without a clear answer at quarterback, Taylor is the living embodiment of that meme where the Lamborghini is sitting in the driveway of the trailer park. He was most valuable to Indy as a trade chip at the deadline, and that remains the case this offseason. The only difference is that any team acquiring him is getting a back that's a little older, has a little more mileage, and doesn't help them for this stretch run in 2026. That sets up a possibly diminished return this offseason if/when the Colts deal him compared to what they could've gotten at this deadline. For a team that won't have its first-round pick in 2027 after trading for Sauce Gardner at last year's deadline, they were in a position to refill the cupboard. Neither Jones nor Taylor likely would've fetched a first-rounder, but they would've given Indy premium ammunition for a later deal that could vault them back up. That level of asset mismanagement around the deadline now has the potential to ripple beyond just this second half of the season. Jones being waived is just one of the initial steps that the Colts will take as they embark on this rebuild and they tripped out of the gate. Whether it's firing Shane Steichen, trading Taylor, or eventually hiring a new GM (if they can find a taker), the organization needs to have a more definitive and realistic plan for its future so they're not looking back with major second guesses like they currently are following this deadline.

title: UCLA's Cori Close echoes Geno Auriemma, laments state of roster building: 'There is something wrong' - CBS Sports
description: UCLA had six seniors drafted into the WNBA last season and 'all took pay cuts,' Close said
body:
UCLA had six seniors drafted into the WNBA last season and 'all took pay cuts,' Close said
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 20, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:39 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        LOS ANGELES -- Earlier this week, UConn women's basketball coach Geno Auriemma went viral for criticizing the new norm of paying high school recruits seven figures in NIL money when they haven't "dribbled the ball one time in college." He is not the only one who feels NIL has complicated the process of building a roster and that perhaps there should be more regulations.On Thursday, UCLA signed No. 2 overall recruit Ivanna Wilson Manyacka, who became the third top-25 player Bruins coach Cori Close has added from the class of 2027. Close and her staff are setting up the program for future success, but she still spoke candidly about how she thinks the current state of NIL feels "off." "I think the number should go down, to be honest," Close told CBS Sports. "When you're talking about that, you are talking about players getting paid more than A'ja Wilson, who is arguably one of the best players in the world. There is something wrong when our six seniors that all got drafted all took pay cuts to go to the WNBA. Something is off with that."Close's comments echo Auriemma, who said he doesn't understand why there are players coming straight out of high school making more than the majority of WNBA players. 
Close has previously stated she feels like a CEO of a company just as much as a basketball coach. She described that scenario again this week while explaining that, for her staff, all recruiting decisions have to be "intentional" and "strategic" because it is all an investment. Which decision will pay dividends faster? Which recruits are high-risk investments?
Close said the way recruiting is structured now makes it harder for coaches to wait for young players to develop because there are a "limited amount of resources," so now coaches can seldom take a chance on someone, which can limit opportunities for some athletes. UCLA is only going to recruit freshmen who can be "difference-makers," Close said. Otherwise, Close will fill out her roster through the transfer portal. "The developmental age of developing freshmen over a two- or three-year period, it just doesn't work anymore. We have to have a balance of swinging for the fences on really impactful freshmen and if we don't get those, we go to the portal," Close said. 
"The problem is that we don't have a system that has really been thought through [where] there is accountability, there's transparency, that can have us be a healthy model. Until that time, it's keeping up with the Joneses. No one likes it, but who is going to be the one to say, 'Oh well, we are not gonna compete for the best players.' It's a really hard thing. Until we have a really healthy system with good boundaries, this is what we're going to be left with."

title: NBA injury updates: The latest on Tyrese Haliburton, Anthony Edwards, Kawhi Leonard, Dylan Harper, more - CBS Sports
description: The barrage of injuries to high-profile players has been one of the stories of the NBA season so far
body:
The barrage of injuries to high-profile players has been one of the stories of the NBA season so far
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 20, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:35 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Injuries have been one of the defining stories of the young 2026-27 NBA season, and while some teams like the Oklahoma City Thunder are unfortunately months away from relief, others are beginning to see a light at the end of the health tunnel. We're now nearly a month or so out from the early-season wave of losses, and on Friday, ESPN's Shams Charania gave updates on the health of several key absent players. Let's use that as a launching point to check in on a handful of injured stars.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Tyrese Haliburton, PacersIt took Indiana's star point guard a full season to recover from the torn Achilles tendon he suffered in Game 7 of the 2025 NBA Finals, but sadly, his return lasted just four games before he headed back to the sideline. Haliburton was diagnosed with a left hamstring strain in October, and according to ESPN, he will be sidelined for at least the next couple of weeks. For now, there is no firmer timeline than that, with Pacers coach Rick Carlisle saying in a recent radio interview that he didn't think it was "out of the question" that Haliburton would play in November, but he would not "put a hard date on anything." Haliburton looked mostly like himself in the four games he played early this season, averaging just under 22 points and 10 assists. The Pacers have fallen to 5-10 and the Eastern Conference's No. 10 seed without him, and they are seemingly aware of the need for reinforcements. The Pacers "clearly are looking at doing something" on the trade market, with an upgrade on the wing viewed as a strong possibility, Jake Fischer said Friday on SiriusXM NBA Radio.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Anthony Edwards, TimberwolvesA return to action seems further off for Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards, who had knee surgery in late October. Edwards spoke with reporters Thursday and said he has "no clue" when he'll be able to return to the floor and declined to offer a timetable, per ESPN.Edwards missed 21 games last year and dealt with a knee issue in the postseason. Despite a hot start, that included a 47-point outburst against the Cavaliers, Edwards continued to experience discomfort in the knee, prompting the team to choose the surgery route rather than have their superstar continue playing through pain. "It needed to be done in order for me to be able to play without any pain for the next couple years," Edwards said. "But who knows? Maybe in a couple years I might have to get something else. But hopefully not. I think I'll be pretty good."
Led by LaMelo Ball, the Wolves have excelled even in Edwards' absence. At 11-5, Minnesota sits at No. 5 in the Western Conference standings entering their game against the Grizzlies on Saturday. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Kawhi Leonard, RaptorsLeonard has played just twice this season due to knee swelling, but according to Charania, there is optimism that he will return within the next few weeks. Leonard has been dealing with patellar tendinopathy, more commonly known as "jumper's knee," TSN reported on Tuesday. That is the same issue he dealt with throughout his 2019 championship season. SportsNet confirmed that reporting, while noting that swelling is not typically how that injury presents. SportsNet's reporting indicates that the swelling and jumper's knee are separate issues.The good news on this front is that the reporting to this point indicates that the Raptors do not expect these issues to linger once Leonard returns. Toronto successfully managed Leonard's health through that title season, and is being cautious to start this year as well. However, his absence has certainly been felt as Toronto is in the midst of a six-game losing streak without him.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Brandon Ingram, ClippersMeanwhile, the player Leonard was traded for is just about ready to make his Clippers debut. Brandon Ingram is expected to return Monday against the Houston Rockets, according to Charania. Ingram suffered a partially torn Achilles tendon last season, which kept him out of the Clippers' lineup at the start of this year. His absence has been keenly felt in Los Angeles as the Clippers have scuttled to a 4-10 start without him. Los Angeles has both a bottom-eight offense and defense so far this season, so getting Ingram on the court should represent a helpful talent infusion.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Dylan Harper, SpursSan Antonio's second-year star thankfully avoided a major injury when he fell on the court against the Clippers on Thursday. He will, however, miss 1-3 weeks with a left hip rotator strain. Harper was walking without a limp following the injury, per The San Antonio Express-News, a positive sign for his recovery.The Spurs have the NBA's best record at 13-3, but the story to watch as Harper rests is the performance of former All-Star De'Aaron Fox. Just beginning a four-year max contract, Fox has scored just 23 points in his last three games combined. He's averaging the fewest points and assists of his career since his rookie season. The Spurs had been starting their three high-profile guards -- Fox, Harper and Stephon Castle -- together early in the season. It was working, but with the caveat that that group never played a second without Victor Wembanyama. The Spurs are more than 40 points per 100 possessions better when their MVP candidate is on the floor.
If Fox can't right the ship while Harper is out, that could open the door to San Antonio moving him to the bench upon Harper's return. The Spurs thrived last season with two ball-handlers, two shooters and Wembanyama in their starting lineup. The three guards are working because basically anything works with Wembanyama, but when the competition gets stiffer in the playoffs, it's going to be harder to get away with so little shooting in the starting lineup. That puts the onus on Fox to prove he still belongs in the starting lineup, and bouncing back while Harper is out will be a big part of that.

With Reed struggling mightily in 2026, Texas A&M is likely turning over the reins to Brady Hart for the clash with the Sooners

                    at
    4:32 pm ET
                        
                •

        Brady Hart is currently expected to get his first career start for Texas A&M on Saturday against Oklahoma, sources confirmed to CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz and Chris Hummer. The anticipated move comes after multi-year starter Marcel Reed struggled in last week's 22-7 loss vs. Tennessee, finishing 9-of-22 passing for 71 yards and an interception.A sophomore out of Cocoa Beach, Florida, Hart is 14 of 25 for 165 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions across appearances in four games. He threw both interceptions against LSU and Tennessee.Hart came into the game with 2:44 left at Kyle Field against Tennessee and received a roaring ovation after completing his first pass attempt for a first down to Mario Craver.Hart signed with Texas A&M in December 2024 after flipping his commitment from Michigan and reclassifying from the 2026 class to the previous cycle. Texas A&M pursued Hart after Husan Longstreet flipped his pledge from the Aggies to USC.
Texas A&M ranks 13th in the SEC in total offense, scoring offense, explosive plays and 15th in passing offense. Only Arch Manning and Sam Leavitt have thrown more interceptions than Reed, who's had two fewer attempts than the Texas quarterback and 53 fewer than LSU's starter.The Aggies chose to retain Reed this offseason after the dual-threat quarterback helped Texas A&M reach the College Football Playoff last fall for the first time in program history, despite struggling down the stretch. This season, the offense never got off the ground with Reed in charge under first-year OC Holmon Wiggins, who Mike Elko promoted this offseason from his previous stint as wide receivers coach.Hart might be the spark that Texas A&M (4-6) needs to reach bowl eligibility. The Aggies must beat the Sooners this weekend and upset Texas in Week 13 to get to the necessary six-win threshold.
CBS Sports reported earlier this week that the Aggies and Reed would likely part ways this offseason as both parties look to start fresh in 2027. If Reed heads to the bench against Oklahoma as expected, his season concludes with below-average numbers — 1,172 yards passing, eight touchdowns, nine interceptions and a completion rate of 55.7%.After rushing for six touchdowns and nearly 500 yards as a junior, Reed has just 206 yards and three scores this fall."Our offense is inept," Elko said after last week's performance against Tennessee. "I don't know how you can put this on one kid. It's on me. It's a completely nonfunctional offense. Come after me."
Elko called the team's offensive production pathetic following its sixth loss this season, but has not placed Reed under the microscope ... until now. Throwing Hart to the wolves against the Sooners means matching up with the SEC's fifth-best defense (294.6 yards per game).

title: Miami star WR Malachi Toney 'really close' to returning from ankle injury, Mario Cristobal says - CBS Sports
description: The Hurricanes may get their All-American playmaker back very soon before the College Football Playoff
body:
The Hurricanes may get their All-American playmaker back very soon before the College Football Playoff
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 20, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:07 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Miami might be getting standout wide receiver Malachi Toney back to its lineup earlier than expected, coach Mario Cristobal revealed Friday on "The Pat McAfee Show." The All-American candidate, who missed the Hurricanes' loss at Notre Dame and their 36-25 win over Duke after ankle surgery earlier this month, is "really close," according to Cristobal.Initial best-case estimates suggested Miami was preparing to have Toney back for its postseason run, but now the ACC's top playmaker could return for the conference title game if the Hurricanes secure a berth this weekend against Virginia Tech."I think the best part about it is that he is being very proactive about not being a distraction," Cristobal said. "He knows he's not playing right now, and he's gotta coach and encourage and push his teammates to be their very best while he gets prepared to play."Before his injury, Toney recorded 73 receptions for 1,027 yards and 13 touchdowns to lead the conference and was on pace to eclipse last season's record-setting numbers set as a true freshman.
Toney hurt his ankle in practice a few days before Miami's only loss of the season against the Fighting Irish."Obviously, losing a guy like Malachi hurts, but especially during the week, mid-game plan hurts even more," Miami wideout Cooper Barkate said after his team's win over Duke. "So, yeah, I think it was a little bit a little better coming into this week, knowing what we had and planning for success."Without Toney in the lineup, Shannon Dawson has been forced to scale back Miami's downfield passing game a bit in the last two games. Per 247Sports, Mensah is coming off a performance against Duke in which he threw for 382 yards and one touchdown with an average depth of target of 5.2 yards.
ACC defenses are going man against the Hurricanes, forcing other options behind Toney to try and beat them in single coverage. Despite not having the Heisman contender in the lineup, Miami owns college football's top-ranked scoring offense (averaging 44.1 points per game), ranks fourth in yards per game (518.1) and second in yards per play (7.42). Dawson said he sees the fans' frustrations on social media, angered by the Hurricanes' lack of explosion in the passing game without the sophomore."You have to be patient when defenses are playing a certain way," Dawson said. "I would love to throw a 70-yard touchdown every play. Is that realistic? I mean, some of our fans obviously think so, but the reality is [the defenses] have a say in the matter. If they're going to play a certain way, I can throw vertical every time if we want to go three-and-out. That's the easy way for me to get fired. That's exactly what they want — some of them."
Miami initially dropped six spots in the CFP Rankings from its top spot after its loss to Notre Dame. CFP chair Hunter Yurachek has said in each of the last two weeks after the reveal that the selection committee still "likes" the Hurricanes, who have "a lot of talent on that team with or without Malachi Toney."

title: Daniel Jones released by Colts: Why QB's contract almost ensures he'll clear waivers, be free agent - CBS Sports
description: Indianapolis waived Jones after the club's 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday night
body:
Indianapolis waived Jones after the club's 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday night
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 20, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:40 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Daniel Jones era in Indianapolis didn't make it to the end of Year 2. The Colts cut their run with the veteran quarterback short, waiving him in the aftermath of a 26-3 defeat at the hands of the Houston Texans in Week 11. While cutting ties at this juncture was shocking for the Colts, a divorce seemed inevitable this offseason as the team is 3-8 with Jones as a main culprit of the organization's shortcomings. His 15 turnovers are the most in the NFL, and his 13 interceptions set a new career-high. Thursday's loss was also his sixth straight game with an interception, which is the longest streak by a Colts player since Curtis Painter in 2011.That's not the version of Jones the Colts were hoping to get when they signed him to a two-year, $88 million contract extension back in March. They had hoped Jones would return to the player he was over the first eight games of the 2025 season, prior to suffering a season-ending Achilles tear. Over that stretch, Jones had the Colts at 7-1 while boasting a 109.5 passer rating. However, that flash in the pan was just that. Jones was unable to recapture that magic, and Indianapolis is now left paying a hefty price. 
Below, we'll explain some financial ramifications regarding the Colts waiving Jones, what his contract says and why it'd be extremely surprising for a team to claim him before he clears waivers on Monday. 
Colts clear cap space by waiving Daniel Jones For 2027, the final year of Jones' extension, the quarterback was set to have a $46.8 million cap hit. By waiving him, Indy will actually clear about $11.6 million in space for this offseason as they look for a new signal-caller and replenish the roster. While there are cap savings, Jones will account for $35.2 million in dead money, which is tied to his $44 million signing bonus that was prorated through 2030, according to CBS Sports salary cap expert Joel Corry. Again, this is assuming Jones is waived, which he almost certainly will be (we explain why below). Meanwhile, Spotrac notes that Indy will have paid out $49.8 million to Jones for 11 games this season. Ouch.
Why Daniel Jones will likely clear waiversJones is now subject to waivers until Monday at 4 p.m. ET. Any team in the league can put in a claim for the veteran quarterback, but it's highly unlikely that'll be the case. Why? Any team that claims Jones would take on $2 million for the rest of this season and $38 million in non-guaranteed money in 2027, as noted by NFL Network. When it comes to 2027, $6.5 million of Jones' base salary and a $4 million roster bonus are guaranteed for injury. So, any team claiming him off of waivers would be on the hook for at least $10.5 million next season. It would be downright shocking to see any club electing to go down that route in a pursuit of Jones at this stage. If they're interested, the more cost-effective move would be for hiim to clear waivers, have the Colts pick up the tab, and sign him as a free agent at a lower number. Then, the hypothetical new team would only be responsible for whatever it signs him for.
